claims.claim: Local 214 represents 1,200 warehouse workers at Kessler Logistics; its lead negotiator is Yolanda Bright.
Kessler Logistics' lead negotiator is Dennis Wozniak, VP of operations, who has authority to accept an agreement up to a 4.5 percent wage increase without board approval.
Bright has authority from a ratification vote to accept any offer at or above a 4 percent wage increase.
The union set a strike deadline of 11:59 PM America/Chicago on 31 October 2026.
As of 26 October the employer's standing offer is a 3.5 percent wage increase and the union's standing demand is 5 percent.
A mediated bargaining session is scheduled for 29 October 2026 at 10:00 AM America/Chicago.
Both negotiators attend mediated sessions in person and hear offers made at the table immediately.
Formulating and tabling a revised offer takes a negotiator roughly 45 minutes of caucus time in comparable sessions.
Wozniak has told the mediator he will move to 4.5 percent, his full authority, only if the union first comes down from 5 percent.
Bright has told her executive board she is prepared to come down to 4.5 percent at the mediated session to avoid a strike.
An agreement is recorded as accepted when a negotiator accepts the other side's tabled offer at the table.
